chunk_findings.detail: The new spec gives contradictory stop rules. Rule 2 says that when `ddflow next` exits 2 with nothing ready, that is completion, the orchestrator should report it and stop, and explicitly says this is *not* one of the question gates in rule 5. Rule 5 then says the orchestrator must “Stop ONLY where the question tool says so” and that “Everything else carries the wave forward.” Given a scope that becomes empty, the agent is simultaneously required to stop and forbidden to stop; in practice this can make it either loop re-reading an empty `ddflow next` or terminate in violation of the stated stop invariant.
chunk_findings.title: .kilo/agent/ddflow-orchestrator.md:24,34

chunk_findings.detail: Rule 7 only assesses ddflow “at the end of each wave and before any compaction,” but the project self-assessment rule requires assessment at the end of every agent run, phase, and before compaction [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. If the orchestrator reaches an operator approval, policy decision, or other question/operator gate and stops mid-wave (allowed by rule 5), there is no “end of wave” or compaction trigger, so any ddflow bug or missing feature encountered in that partial run is not filed.
chunk_findings.title: .kilo/agent/ddflow-orchestrator.md:40

chunk_findings.detail: The Kilo orchestration spec persists the wave position under a single fixed memory key `orchestrator_wave`, while `.kilo/command/ddflow-wave.md` launches background orchestrator subtasks for arbitrary `$1` scopes. If an operator starts `/ddflow-wave phase-1` and then starts `/ddflow-wave bugs` before the first background wave has finished, both orchestrators use the same `orchestrator_wave` persistence slot. The second wave overwrites the first wave's stored ready-set/position, so when the first wave resumes after a background process or `ddflow wait`, it can fan items from the wrong scope or conclude the first scope is done. That contradicts the command's promise that the orchestrator "drives exactly that scope to empty"; the persisted wave position needs to be scoped by the requested scope/run id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/kilo.toml:[orchestration].persist

chunk_findings.detail: The description advertises that the command accepts "item ids" plural, but the command interface and body are singular: `argument-hint: <phase-id | bugs | item-id>` and the body only interpolates `$1`. If an operator follows the description and runs `/ddflow-wave item-1 item-2`, only the first positional token (`item-1`) is passed as the scope; `item-2` is silently ignored (or rejected if the hint is enforced), so the command does not drive the advertised multi-item scope to empty.
chunk_findings.title: .kilo/command/ddflow-wave.md:2

chunk_findings.detail: The completion test is “exit 2 from `ddflow next` with nothing ready”, but the same rule explicitly says held/blocked items remain in the scope and are handled later. Given a scope whose remaining items are all held (for example, blocked by another agent’s lease or by the parallelism cap), `ddflow next` can produce no ready items and exit 2; line 20 then tells the orchestrator to report completion and stop, leaving those held/blocked items unprocessed instead of waiting/re-reading. The stop condition must be based on the scope being empty overall, not merely on the ready set being empty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:20

chunk_findings.detail: The delta says “The wave position goes to Kilo memory so a compaction or restart resumes at the wave, never before it,” while the same bullet says “Never wrap the mission in a foreground session goal: `goal start` IS the loop that blocks the operator chat.” Memory alone is only state, not a continuation mechanism. Given a Kilo process restart after a wave position has been persisted, the background `/ddflow-wave` subagent is gone and the delta provides no goal loop, scheduled wakeup, or `ddflow wait` hook to re-invoke the orchestrator, so the wave stalls instead of resuming.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/kilo-cline.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The fanout instruction changed from “one claimed item each” to “one ready item each” and no longer tells the orchestrator to claim each item before spawning `task` subagents. If two `/ddflow-wave` drivers, or a driver and another agent, read the same `ddflow next --json` ready set and follow this wording literally, they can both select the same unclaimed item and fan it out to subagents, causing duplicate implementation and conflicting merges.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/kilo-cline.md:12

chunk_findings.detail: The change directs `ddflow adopt` to know and write Kilo-specific filesystem layout (`.kilo/command/ddflow-wave.md` and `.kilo/agent/ddflow-orchestrator.md`) from the adopt command path (`_write_harness_files`), rather than through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. For example, if Kilo changes its command/agent directory layout, the failure is demonstrated by `ddflow adopt` still writing the hard-coded `.kilo/command/` and `.kilo/agent/` paths from the adopt service; swapping or testing that harness layout cannot be done by replacing an adapter port. This embeds an external filesystem-layout dependency outside the adapter layer, violating [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/kilo-cline.md (new `[orchestration]` / `ddflow adopt` prose; see also `_commands.py:_write_harness_files`)

chunk_findings.detail: The orchestrator is told that `ddflow next --json` exiting 2 with nothing ready means “the scope is empty” and to report completion and stop. But the same wave rule says `held`/`blocked` items are not ready and should be handled later after merges or park. A scope with only `held`/`blocked` items (dependencies, leases, parallelism cap) will therefore be treated as empty and abandoned, leaving those items unprocessed. The previous wording “the wave is empty” was compatible with a no-ready-but-held/blocked state; changing it to “scope is empty” is a regression.
chunk_findings.title: .kilo/agent/ddflow-orchestrator.md:2 (exit 2 bullet)

chunk_findings.detail: The command frontmatter still declares `agent: ddflow-orchestrator` and `subtask: true`, so invoking `/ddflow-wave` already runs the `ddflow-orchestrator` subagent as a background subtask. The new body then instructs that subagent to “Run the `ddflow-orchestrator` subagent as a BACKGROUND subtask,” which makes the orchestrator spawn another orchestrator for the same scope. This causes recursive orchestration/duplicate wave driving instead of executing the wave loop in the current subtask.
chunk_findings.title: .kilo/command/ddflow-wave.md body

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s own intent specifies the Claude Code instantiation is “Claude Code Task,” but this TOML sets `dispatch = "Agent (worktree isolation, model explicit)"`. A generator consuming this orchestration data will emit the wrong Claude Code dispatch tool, so ready items cannot be fanned out on the Claude Code harness.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml [orchestration].dispatch

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s intent specifies the opencode instantiation is “opencode subtask,” but this TOML sets `dispatch = "opencode config/zen agent (one item each)"`. The generated opencode orchestration instructions will use a dispatch mechanism that does not match the intended harness-specific subtask behavior, breaking wave fanout for opencode.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/opencode.toml [orchestration].dispatch

chunk_findings.detail: The new subagent branch calls `_write_command(repo, dst, templates / src, "agents")`. The diff does not update `_write_command`; all existing call sites, including the command branch immediately above this one, call it with exactly three arguments. When `adopt` processes any harness that has a `[subagents].files` entry (Kilo is added in this change), this call passes an extra positional argument and raises `TypeError: _write_command() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given`, aborting adoption before the subagent files are emitted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_commands.py:_write_harness_files

chunk_findings.detail: The orchestration validation only checks that `loop` is in `ORCHESTRATION_LOOPS`; it never requires `dispatch`, `wait`, `persist`, or `stop`. A harness descriptor like `[orchestration] loop = "background-subagents"` with all other orchestration keys omitted passes validation, producing an `Orchestration` instance with empty strings for the fan-out, wait, persistence, and stop primitives. The whole purpose of this change is to emit harness orchestrator files from this record, so accepted incomplete data will generate blank/missing primitive instructions and break the emitted wave driver.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:193

chunk_findings.detail: The orchestrator treats `exit 2` from `ddflow next` with “nothing ready” as proof the scope is empty and stops. But line 20 of the same file says `held`/`blocked` items are still in scope and just come later. So a scope whose remaining items are all `held`/`blocked` (dependencies, leases, parallelism cap) can produce a `next` read with no ready items; line 22 then tells the orchestrator to report completion and stop even though no item has completed. That violates the stated loop contract (stop only on a question/operator gate) and silently abandons remaining work. The completion condition must require no `ready`, `held`, or `blocked` items — not just “nothing ready”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:22

chunk_findings.detail: The command advertises `item ids` (plural) as a valid scope, but the body only forwards `$1`. Given `/ddflow-wave 101 102`, the orchestrator receives only `101`, and `102` is silently excluded from the scope. Either forward `$@`/`$ARGUMENTS` or change the argument hint and body to a single item id so the documented batch scope is actually supported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/commands/kilo/ddflow-wave.md:9

chunk_findings.detail: The new text says “Never wrap the mission in a foreground session goal: `goal start` IS the loop that blocks the operator chat” and replaces the loop with a background `/ddflow-wave` orchestrator subtask. This contradicts the change intent, which specifies the Kilo harness instantiation as “Kilo session goal + task subagent.” A Kilo agent following this emitted delta will not use `goal start`, so the required session-goal mechanism for the orchestration record is not instantiated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/kilo-cline.md: item 1

chunk_findings.detail: The previous explicit stop rule— “Stop ONLY where the question tool says so: operator approvals … policy decisions, an un-settleable review finding”— is deleted and no replacement stop condition is stated. The new text only says long gates are waits, never stops. Given a wave where `ddflow next --json` returns an empty ready set after merges/park, an agent following this delta is not told it must keep waiting; it may stop without a question or operator gate, violating the orchestration spec’s “stop ONLY on a question or operator gate.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/kilo-cline.md: item 1

chunk_findings.detail: The added line breaks the inline code span for the command: it writes `` `ddflow next `` with an opening backtick but no closing backtick before the newline, then continues with `` --json ``, and the next backtick occurs only before `` `tier:fast|balanced|deep` ``. A Markdown renderer will consume the intervening sentence as code span content, so the emitted VS Code driver spec no longer displays the command `` ddflow next --json `` as intended, and the following `` `tier:fast|balanced|deep` `` span is also mangled. This is a functional defect in the generated spec, not just cosmetics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/vscode.md item 2

chunk_findings.detail: The emitted driver deltas state “the wave position is ddflow's own committed event log” (opencode item 1 and vscode item 2), but the change’s intent explicitly requires the ORCHESTRATION record to include “position persistence” and says the hand-written orchestrator “persist[s] the wave position in memory.” Those are different mechanisms: the in-memory cursor is the orchestrator’s own wave position, while the committed event log is ddflow’s durable event stream. The emitted docs therefore instruct harnesses to rely on the event log instead of maintaining the required in-memory position cursor, which contradicts the requested orchestration data and can make the background loop resume from the wrong wave position after a stop or restart.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/opencode.md and docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/vscode.md

chunk_findings.detail: `_write_harness_files` is imported from `._commands` in `ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py` line 8, but `_commands.py` (which is modified in this change) only defines `_write_command` and other helpers without defining or exposing `_write_harness_files`, leading to an `ImportError: cannot import name '_write_harness_files' from '.commands'` when `_adopt.py` runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_adopt.py:88
